IR.rationale: A hawkish repricing of the US policy path along the 5-year segment raises the global discount rate and pulls capital out of emerging markets. The absence of such repricing is the state that is benign for EM equity returns.

B.rationale: Strong EM sovereign bond returns alongside stable US corporate spreads describe easy external financing for emerging economies. Such conditions tend to carry over into EM equity returns.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility signals a high price of risk. It tends to be followed by higher subsequent equity returns as the risk premium is earned.

AP.rationale: US equity returns lead international markets because information diffuses gradually. A strong US week not yet matched by EM equities therefore signals catch-up potential.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically occur when beaten-down, high-beta assets rebound. That regime favours risky segments such as EM equities.

FX.rationale: A soft dollar together with a strong commodity currency marks global risk-on and eases EM dollar-debt burdens. Both support EM equity returns.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices improve the terms of trade and earnings of commodity-exporting emerging markets.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions coincide with elevated required returns. Subsequent returns are higher on average as conditions normalise.

ENDG.rationale: Equity index returns show time-series momentum at intermediate horizons. Recent strength therefore carries some information about continued gains.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in US intermediate yields relative to the policy rate trigger capital-flow reversals from emerging markets. These reversals raise EM equity volatility.

B.rationale: Widening corporate spreads combined with weak EM sovereign bonds signal deteriorating credit risk appetite. This state precedes turbulence in risky assets.

V.rationale: Implied volatility is forward-looking. It contains information about future realised variance beyond what past realised variance already shows.

AP.rationale: Through leverage and volatility-feedback effects, negative equity returns raise subsequent volatility more than positive returns do.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns cluster in panic and rebound phases, when market volatility is elevated and persistent.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength together with yen appreciation reflects safe-haven flows and carry unwinds. Both accompany turbulent EM markets.

COM.rationale: Oil price slumps hit exporter economies and signal weak global demand. Both raise EM equity volatility.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress reflects funding strains and deleveraging that spill over into volatility in risky asset markets.

ENDG.rationale: Variance is highly persistent, so recent high realised variance signals that the volatility regime will continue.

IR.rationale: A sharp repricing toward faster US tightening at the short end raises the risk of sudden stops in EM capital flows and sharp sell-offs.

B.rationale: Simultaneous widening of US credit spreads and losses on EM sovereign debt mark a credit risk-off state. Equity crashes are more likely in this state.

V.rationale: High market fear combined with high policy uncertainty widens the left tail of the return distribution.

AP.rationale: Weak recent EM returns signal deteriorating risk appetite and raise the odds of further tail losses through deleveraging.

ST.rationale: Momentum underperformance indicates unstable, high-volatility regimes in which large market moves in either direction are more frequent.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar tightens financing for EM dollar borrowers and coincides with capital outflows. This raises crash risk.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices worsen EM terms of trade and fiscal positions. This raises the probability of large equity losses.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions are associated with fat left tails in future returns, consistent with the growth-at-risk literature.

ENDG.rationale: Recent weakness signals a stressed regime in which further large losses are more likely because volatility clusters.

IR.rationale: Falling US intermediate yields relative to the policy rate ease global financing conditions. This can trigger strong inflows into EM equities.

B.rationale: Strong EM sovereign bond rallies signal compressing EM risk premia, which tend to accompany large equity gains.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens both tails. Large relief rallies are most frequent after fear spikes.

AP.rationale: Strong US equity returns lead global markets and raise the chance of a large subsequent EM gain.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes coincide with sharp rebounds of beaten-down high-beta assets, a group that includes EM equities.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar together with commodity-currency strength marks a global reflation and risk-on state that favours large EM gains.

COM.rationale: Commodity rallies boost exporter earnings and EM sentiment, fattening the right tail of returns.

MC.rationale: Large gains cluster in high-stress periods as markets rebound once stress abates.

ENDG.rationale: After sell-offs, high volatility and elevated risk premia make sharp rebounds more likely.
